text: Which of the following is an important purpose of a Use Case diagram?

options.text: To define the sequences of actions performed by the user

explanation: Identification of functional requirements is an important purpose of a Use Case diagram.

text: In an Online Food Delivery application, which of the following can be valid Use Cases?
explanation: Among all the options, Track order, Place order, and View food menu are valid use cases.

text: Which of the following statements describe valid characteristics of a Use Case in UML?

options.text: Represents a sequence of interactions that achieve a goal
Must always be implemented as a software module
Describes system behavior from an external perspective
Always corresponds to a UI screen

explanation: Use case represents a sequence of interactions, Describes system behavior from an external prespective and use case initiated by an actor.

text: Which of the following are characteristics of a well-formed use case scenario?

options.text: Focuses on achieving a meaningful goal for the actor
Specifies the system’s internal implementation details
Describes interactions between the actor and the system
It is written in clear, simple language understandable to stakeholders
Lists all UI controls the actor must click

explanation: A use case must represent a goal that provides value to the actor. A scenario outlines step-by-step interactions between the actor and the system. Scenarios must be readable and understandable by business and technical stakeholders.

text: Consider the following part of a use case model: Which of the following can be inferred?

options.text: Use case Verify Email may be optionally executed during execution of Register Account
Use case Register Account may be optionally executed during execution of Verify Email
Use case Verify Email will be compulsorily executed during execution of Register Account
Use case Register Account will be compulsorily executed during execution of Verify Email
Whenever the use case Register Account is executed, Verify Email use case will also be executed

explanation: Register Account include Verify E-mail Use case. So, Verify Email will be compulsorily executed during execution of Register Account. And also whenever the use case Register Account is executed, Verify Email use case will also be executed

text: Usually a textual description accompanies a use case diagram. Which of the following are hallmarks of a poor textual description?

options.text: Use case description starts with a request from the system to an actor.
Use case description ends with the system producing all answers the actor asked for.
Use case description is a narrative essay of the actor inputs and the system outputs
Use case description is written from the actor’s point of view.
Use case description details of the internal activities that the system must perform to produce all the required system responses.

explanation: Use case description provides a high-level behavior of the system, user goals, external entities: actors.

text: Which of the following are not true about a use case?

options.text: It is a way in which a system can be used by the users to achieve specific goals
It corresponds to a non-functional requirement.
It defines external behavior without revealing internal structure of system
It is a set of related usage scenarios tied together by a common goal
A use case may have only one scenario of execution
A use case may have zero scenario of execution

explanation: a use case may have many scenarios; Use case diagram represents the important functions in a given system. It identifies external behavior without revealing the internal structure of the system. However, it neither include the non-functional requirements of the system nor does it identify he classes and their interaction.

text: Identification of the different categories of users of a system in its use case diagram does not help towards which of the followings?

options.text: Design of security and authentication mechanism

explanation: Identifies different categories of users: Helps in implementing appropriate interfaces for each category of users. Helps in preparing appropriate documents (e.g. user’s manual). Design of security for different users.

text: Which of the following are not mechanisms supported in UML to factor a complex use case into simpler use cases?
explanation: Three ways of factoring use cases: Generalization-specialization, include and extend.

text: Assume that an academic institute automation software is to be developed. The students need to register at the start of every semester. However, the registration process of the post graduate (PG) students is slightly different than the undergraduate students, since the UG students can register only for the core courses, whereas the PG students are allowed to register for electives. Also, the PG students need to provide their bank account number for payment of monthly stipend and also need to sign an undertaking for doing teaching assistantship. Which one of the following mechanisms should be deployed to factor the student registration into UG registration and PG registration?
explanation: From the question we can observe that UG and PG student’s registration process is similar but slightly different. So, we can use here inheritance to factor the student registration into UG and PG registration.

text: Suppose a library automation software is to be designed. In this, one of the requirements is that before a book can be issued, it needs to be checked whether the book has been reserved by any user. Which one of the following mechanisms is most appropriate to factor the corresponding use case into issue book and check reservation use cases?
explanation: Use case Issue Book → includes → Check Reservation This means Check Reservation is always executed whenever Issue Book runs. studentRegistration UG PG

text: Which of the following UML mechanisms can be used to separate optional behavior from a base use case?
explanation: «extend» represents behavior that is optional or conditionally executed beyond the base use case.

text: Consider the following use case diagram. Which one of the following is implied by the given use case diagram?

options.text: Check membership validity use case will be invoked during execution of the reserve book use case
Reserve Book use case may be invoked during execution of the Check membership validity use case
Check membership validity use case may be invoked during execution of the Reserve book use case
Reserve book use case may optionally be invoked during execution of the Check membership validity use case
To execute Reserve book use case the user needs to first execute the Check membership validity use case

explanation: From the notation in the diagram Check membership validity use case is a common use case, whereas Reserve book is the base class. The base class must be include the common class.

text: Which one of the following about a subclass should be always true?

options.text: It has more attributes than its superclass
It has more operations than its superclass
It redefines the behavior of its superclass
It is a specialization of its superclass
It is a generalization of its superclass

explanation: A subclass inherits the methods and instance data of its superclasses, and is related to its superclasses by an is-a relationship. A subclass is a special form of the superclass.

text: Which of the following styles of documenting a Use Case diagram are not recommended?

options.text: A use case name should begin with a noun
An actor should be associated with exactly one use cases
Actors are associated with one or more use cases
Use arrows to represent the actor-use case relationship
Show interaction of actors with each other.

explanation: Please refer slide no.2 of week 2 lecture material.

text: Which part of an association represented between two classes in a UML class diagram defines how many objects of that class may be linked with a single object of the other class involved in the association?
explanation: Multiplicity is the number of objects from one class that relate with a single object in an associated class.

text: Which one of the following sentences most closely describes "multiple inheritance"?

options.text: Two classes inherit from each other
A base class has two or more derived classes
A class has both parent and grand parent classes
A child class has two or more parent classes
A child class has both an "is a" and a "has a" relationship with its parent class

explanation: Multiple inheritance means that a subclass can inherit from two or more superclasses.

text: Suppose in a course management software, as soon as a student completes course registration, the billing information is submitted to an external billing system to handle billing and collection of payment. Which one of the following use case diagrams correctly models this?
explanation: The correct use case diagram is A.

text: Consider the following class diagram. What is the visibility of the method totalAmount() of the class Invoice?
explanation: UML syntax of protected visibility is #.

text: Consider the following class diagram. What is the visibility of the method updateProfile() of the class UserAccount?
explanation: UML syntax of package-wide is: ~

text: Which one of the following UML class diagrams most accurately models: “A person keeps many animals as pets. But, an animal is owned by a single person.”
explanation: A person keeps many animals as pets. But, an animal is owned by a single person is correctly depicted by figure A of the above diagram

text: Which of the following is implied by the class diagram given below?

options.text: Each Key object has a link to exactly one Door object
Each Key object has a link to many Door objects
Each Door object stores a reference to a Key object
Each Door object has links to many Key objects
Many Door objects have links to many Key objects
Many Door objects have links to exactly one Key object

explanation: This is an one direction association so the correct option is each door object has a link to exactly one door object.

text: How many objects of type File exist for each Directory object?
explanation: File is text file or image file. Text file has 1 associativity and Image file has either 0 or 1associativity. So, the answer is 1 or 2.

text: An interface in UML is:

options.text: A set of objects used to provide a specific behaviour
A set of classes used in a collaboration
A set of attributes used on an operation
A set of operations used to specify a service of a class or component

explanation: In UML modeling, interfaces are model elements that define sets of operations that other model elements, such as classes, or components must implement.

text: Which of the following can be inferred from the following UML class diagram?

options.text: Each Teacher teaches exactly one Student
Each Student has exactly one Teacher
One Teacher teaches one or more Students
One Student is taught by many Teachers

explanation: Both b. and c. are correct for the given diagram based on the multiplicity.

text: In which of the following, the attributes of the association relation between two classes is made into a separate class?
explanation: The attributes of a association relation between two classes is made in a association class which represents association between classes. Please refer slide no: 15-17 of week 3 lecture material,

text: Which of the following sentences can be inferred from the following UML class diagram?

options.text: A Person may be employed in 0 or 1 Company
A person may work for a single company
A company may employ only one Person
A company may employ zero Persons

explanation: A person has either one employment or no employment. So, except option c. all are correct.

explanation: Figure A represents the give code segment. Please refer slide 47 of week 3 lecture material for more details.

explanation: From the given code we can understand one Advertiser can have one account. So, option a. is correct.

text: Consider that the class Student is associated to the class Course. A Java program implementing the classes is given below. From this diagram, the multiplicity of the association at the Course end of the class diagram can be most appropriately be inferred to be which one of the following.
explanation: From the code segment, it can be inferred that a student can enroll up to 5 courses. Therefore, from the options, the cardinality as Course class is 1..5.

text: Consider the following Java code. Which one of the following class diagrams is equivalent to the given Java code?
explanation: The code represents a qualified association. So, option a. class diagram is the correct representation of the code.

text: Consider the following class diagram depicting the skills acquired by a person, and the competency level for each skill acquired. Given that there are 100 person objects and 10 skill objects, at most how many competency objects may exist?

options.text: Can only be determined at run time

explanation: For one person there could be maximum 3 skills based on the class diagram. So, for 100 persons maximum 100*3=300 competency objects may exist.

text: Consider the following class diagram. Which one of the following is implied by the class diagram?

options.text: There exists up to one Student for each instance of Roll in a Class.
There exists up to one Roll for each instance of Student in a Class.
Each Student of a Class has a Roll.
Each Student in a Class has at most one Roll.
Some students in a Class may not have a Roll

explanation: The class diagram represents qualified association. The correct one is: There exists up to one student for each instance of Roll in a class

text: Which of the following class diagrams represents “CircularLinkedList class implements all the operations defined by the List interface”.

options.text: All of A, B, and C

explanation: UML provides two equivalent ways of denoting interface relationship. Both A and B represents “CircularLinkedList class implements all the operations defined by the list interface”.

text: Which one of the following features of UML state charts helps reduce repetitive transition specifications and thus minimizes diagram complexity?
explanation: Orthogonal (concurrent) regions allow a state to be divided into multiple independent sub-states that execute in parallel. This avoids drawing many separate transitions between these parallel behaviors. As a result, the state chart becomes cleaner and avoids repetitive transition definitions, reducing overall diagram complexity.

text: Method overloading can be considered to be a form of which one of the following mechanisms?
explanation: Method overloading is an example of static binding. Please refer slide no. 21 to 23 of week 3 lecture material.

text: Consider the following UML state machine diagram. Which of the following can be inferred from the diagram?

The method doIt() must be implemented by Thing2 and Thing3.
The method doIt() must be implemented only by Thing4 andThing5 only.
The method doIt() must be implemented by Thing2, Thing4 and Thing5 only.
There is no need for any class to implement doIt(), because it is already implemented by Thing1.

text: Identify the relation between the two classes Square and Polygon, that can be inferred from the sentence: ‘Square is a polygon.’
explanation: Square is a polygon. So, the relationship is inheritance.

text: Consider the sentence: “A book has many pages”. Which of the following best characterizes the relationship between the Book class and the Page class?
explanation: A book composite of pages. So, option c. is correct.

text: Which one of the following can be said of the method create in the following Java code?
explanation: Here, class circle has three definition of create method. Each one is defined with different number of arguments. So, we can say create is a overloaded method.

text: A state machine diagram is typically used to model the behavior of which one of the following?
explanation: State machine diagrams are used for modeling class objects with complex state-dependent behavior.

text: A car has a Starter switch, two head lights, an Air Conditioning System, and an accelerator pedal. The driver first operates the Starter, then switches on the Lights, then the Air Conditioning System, and finally presses the accelerator pedal. Which pair of diagrams is most useful to model this situation?

options.text: Use case diagram and state machine diagram
Use case diagram and class diagram

explanation: Class Diagram - to show the components of the car (Starter, Headlights, AC System, Accelerator) and their relationships. Sequence Diagram - to show the order of operations performed by the driver on these components.

text: Which of the following statements about state diagrams are correct?

options.text: All actions in a state diagram are attached to transitions
An event may cause an object to remain in the same state it was prior to the event
Once an object leaves a state, it cannot return to that state
Two different transitions out of the same state may be triggered by the same event
An event may not trigger any transitions on a state

explanation: An event may cause an object to remain in the same state it was prior to the event and an event may not trigger any transitions on a state.

text: What is a guard condition in a state diagram?

options.text: An expression comparing the attributes of the modelled objects against the attributes of the associated object.
The condition of a person guarding the state diagram from unwitting destruction by the collaborating designers
A Boolean expression of attribute values which allows state transition only if condition is true
A Boolean expression that allows the transition from the state of the current object into a state of another object in the system
A state activity that protects object attributes from accidental modification by unconditional actions of state transitions

explanation: A guard is a Boolean condition written in square brackets (e.g., [speed > 40]) placed on a transition. The transition is allowed only when the guard evaluates to TRUE. If FALSE, the transition is blocked. So, the correct and standard UML definition is option (c).

text: If a class has 5 state variables, and each of state variable can assume 4 discrete values, what is the maximum number states that an object of the class can assume?
explanation: 5 state variable and 4 discreate values. So, 4^5 =1024

text: Consider the following Java code. Which one of the following sequence diagrams corresponds to the Java code given for class B?
explanation: Figure A represents the state machine diagram of the given code segment.

text: Consider the following sequence diagram. Which methods should be provided in the class Y?
explanation: In class Y, methods doB() and doE() need to implemented.

text: Consider the following sequence diagram. Which one of the following Java code for class B corresponds to the sequence diagram?
explanation: For the given sequence diagram option A represents the correct java code.

text: Consider the following C code. Which one of the following state machine diagrams is encoded by the given code?
explanation: State diagram in A is the correct representation of the given code.

text: In a state machine diagram, which of the following are true?

options.text: Actions are associated with transition and are considered to be processes that occur quickly and are not interruptible.
Actions are associated with transition and are considered to be processes that occur quickly and are interruptible.
Activities are associated with states and can take longer. An activity may be interrupted by some event.
Activities are associated with transition that occur quickly and are not interruptible.
Activities are associated with states and can take longer. An activity cannot be interrupted by any event.

explanation: Option a. and c. are true regarding the state machine diagram.

text: Consider the following state machine model of an overhead projector. Assume that after the initialization, it is noticed that event p occurred. What will be the state of the overhead projector after event occurrence?

options.text: Can be either B or C

explanation: On event P, the state will change to On Floor and Light On states.

text: Consider the following UML state machine for a PrinterController, in which the controller has two concurrent regions: one region controls the paper movement (Feed / Hold), and the other controls the print head (Idle / Printing). The initial pseudostates of the two regions point to Feed and Idle respectively. Which one of the following is the initial starting state of a PrinterController?
explanation: The initial starting states will be Feed and Idle for PrinterController.

text: Which one of the following is FALSE concerning the swim lanes in a UML activity diagram?

options.text: Swimlanes group actions according to the responsible actor or organizational unit.
A swimlane may contain multiple actions connected by control flows.
Control flows may move from one swimlane to another.
An activity diagram must have exactly one swimlane.
Swimlanes are a visual structuring mechanism and do not affect execution semantics.

explanation: An activity diagram may have zero, one, or many swimlanes.

text: Consider the following activity diagram. Which of the following are FALSE regarding the activity diagram.

options.text: Order is an object whose state changes with activity flow
Solid arrows in the diagram are transitions, but dotted arrows are pseudo transitions
The only activity performed by Stockroom is PackOrder
The customer is both the originator and terminator of the sequence of activities.

explanation: The transition between an object parameter and an action state is represented with a dashed line, instead of a solid line. It has the same semantics as normal transition. Here, Order is an object.

text: Which of the following are typical purposes of drawing a UML sequence diagram in object-oriented analysis and design?

options.text: To identify the messages exchanged among collaborating objects in a use case
To elaborate on the ordering of interactions between objects over time
To assign responsibilities to particular objects participating in an interaction
To determine how user interface screens follow each other
To determine the attributes of each class
To illustrate alternative flows and optional interactions using combined fragments

explanation: Sequence diagrams show object interactions and the messages exchanged. They explicitly show time-ordered interactions along the vertical axis. By showing which object sends/receives which message, responsibilities become clear. Sequence diagrams use alt, opt, loop, par, etc., to show variations.

text: Which of the following UML diagrams primarily represent static structure rather than dynamic behavior in an object-oriented design?
explanation: UML diagrams that show static structure focus on the organization of classes, objects, and components, not on runtime behavior.

text: Consider the following UML activity diagram. Which of the following action ordering are not possible by the given activity model?

options.text: Ship order and accept payment are truly concurrent
Make payment and accept payment are truly concurrent

explanation: Accept payment dependent on make payment. So, both are not concurrent. Also, Send Invoice is after Pack Order.

text: Given the following diagram, which method(s) should be implemented for the Account class?
explanation: The methods with incoming edges to the Account class should be implemented by it.

text: Consider the following UML sequence diagram. Based on the given sequence diagram, which one of the following methods should be implemented by the Controller class?
explanation: The methods with incoming edges to the Controller class should be implemented by it.

text: Which of the following UML diagrams, model the dynamic aspects of a system?
explanation: The dynamic model is used to express and model the behaviour of the system over time. It includes support for activity diagrams, state diagrams, sequence diagrams and extensions including business process modelling. So, among all the options, a. and e. are correct.

text: Consider the following fragment of an activity diagram. Based on the semantics of the diagram, which of the following can be TRUE?

options.text: Receive payment is a signal received from an external process
Receive payment is a signal received from another activity in the same process
Receive payment is an object that flows from an external process
Receive payment is a signal that is received asynchronously
Receive payment signal represents an event that triggers the execution of the ship order action without requiring a control flow from the sender.

explanation: Receive payment represent a received signal: Indicates that the activity receives an event from an outside process. Basically, receive payment is a signal. So, option c. is false. And options a. ,b. ,d. , and e. are true.

text: Which one of the following statements about swim lanes in UML activity diagrams is FALSE?

options.text: Swim lanes partition an activity diagram to show which actor is responsible for each action.
The relative ordering of swim lanes determines the order in which actions are executed.
An activity diagram may contain multiple swim lanes.
An action in a swim lane may be associated with a system component rather than a human actor.
Activity and object flows may cross swim lane boundaries.

explanation: Execution order is determined by control flows, decision nodes, fork/join nodes, etc., not by the left-to- right or top-to-bottom placement of swim lanes.

text: Violations of the Open/Closed Principle can be recognized by:

options.text: Classes that are not be inherited, for example final classes in Java.
Classes that contain many private methods.
New public methods get added get added frequently

explanation: The Open/Closed Principle requires that classes be open for extension but closed for modification. Frequent code changes or repeatedly adding new public methods indicate that behavior is being modified directly instead of being extended, which signals an OCP violation.

text: CRC cards are typically used in performing which one of the following activities?
explanation: CRC (Class-Responsibility-Collaboration) cards are used during object-oriented analysis to identify classes and assign responsibilities and collaborations among them. They are not intended for performance tuning, UI design, database normalization, or low-level algorithm design.

text: Which of the following are not valid heuristics for selecting entity classes during object-oriented analysis?

options.text: Nouns that represent persistent information are potential entity classes
Control activities expressed by action verbs typically become entity classes
Temporary input/output data items are good candidates for entity classes
Physical or conceptual things in the problem domain may become entity classes
Every external actor in the use-case model must be converted into an entity class

explanation: Entity classes model long-lived domain information, not control behavior or transient data. Action verbs map to control classes, temporary I/O data should not be entities, and external actors represent roles outside the system rather than domain entities.

text: Which one of the following UML artefacts is generally created earliest during an object-oriented development process to capture the required system behavior from the user’s point of view?
explanation: A use-case diagram is created early in object-oriented development to capture system behavior from the user’s perspective. It focuses on what the system should do, not on how it is internally structured or implemented.

text: What is the number of boundary classes that must be included in the domain model for a software development project whose use case diagram is shown below?
explanation: A boundary class represents the interface between the system and its external actors (users or other systems). It handles input/output, user interactions, and communication, but contains little or no business logic, which is delegated to control or entity classes.

text: What is the number of controller classes required in the domain model for a software development project whose use case diagram is shown below?
explanation: A controller class is responsible for handling system events and coordinating the execution of a use case. It receives input from boundary classes, invokes appropriate domain (entity) objects, and manages the workflow without containing core business logic itself.

text: Suppose a subclass inherits behaviour from a superclass. But, it also introduces few operations that are not at all meaningful for all superclass instances. Then, the design most likely violates which one of the following principles?
explanation: The Liskov Substitution Principle requires that a subclass must be usable wherever its superclass is expected. If a subclass introduces operations that are not meaningful for all superclass instances, substitutability is broken, indicating an LSP violation.

text: Which one of the following is not implied by the dependency inversion principle (DIP)?

options.text: Depend on Abstractions-- not on concretions
Higher-level modules should not depend on the concrete lower-level modules.
Abstractions should not depend on details --- details should depend on abstractions.
Once a class is successfully tested --- it should never change, only extended to meet the requirements changes.

explanation: The Dependency Inversion Principle emphasizes depending on abstractions rather than concrete implementations. Option (e) describes the Open/Closed Principle, not DIP, and therefore is not implied by DIP.

text: In what way is the GUI (graphical user interface) prototype useful in developing a suitable use case model of a software product?

options.text: Packaging of use cases become realistic
Use case test description becomes more structured.

explanation: A GUI prototype primarily helps in realistic packaging of use cases by visualizing related functionalities as they appear to users. It does not reliably make use-case dependencies or test descriptions explicit, which are better derived from behavioral modeling and requirements analysis rather than UI mockups.

text: Consider the following partial description of a Restaurant Automation System (RAS). A restaurant maintains a menu of food items that customers can order. Each food item may be either a vegetarian item or a non-vegetarian item. A customer may create an order that includes multiple food items. A customer may change an ordered item at any time before the order is confirmed. A domain model to be constructed from the above description. Which one of the following is unsuitable to be an entity class in the domain model?
explanation: Entity classes represent persistent domain concepts such as Customer, Order, Food Item, and Menu. “Change” denotes an action or behavior performed on an order, not a long-lived domain object, and therefore is unsuitable as an entity class.

text: Which of the following advantages accrue from separating the user interface from domain model in an application development?

options.text: It makes modifying the user interface easy.
It makes modifying the domain classes easy
It makes the user interface look more friendly.
It enhances the performances of user interface
It allows a user interface developed for one domain model to be easily adapted for another using a different domain model.

explanation: Separating the user interface from the domain model reduces coupling, allowing independent modification of the UI and domain logic. It does not inherently improve UI friendliness, performance, or make a UI easily reusable across different domain models.

text: What is the primary advantage of adhering to the principle: “program to an interface, not to an implementation”?

options.text: Allows to vary the behaviour of the object at runtime.
Allows creating objects only when their operations are requested.
Facilitates performing housekeeping on objects whenever accessed.
Allows to have a local object that will refer to a remote object.
Allows implementing access rights on objects as their operations are requested

explanation: Programming to an interface reduces coupling between clients and concrete implementations. As a result, implementations can change or be replaced without impacting client code, making the system easier to maintain and evolve.

text: Which one of the following GRASP patterns would you use to decide which class is going to handle the user inputs?
explanation: The GRASP Controller pattern assigns responsibility for handling user input and system events to a dedicated controller class. This keeps the user interface separate from domain logic and improves overall design clarity.

text: The expert pattern says assigning the responsibility to fulfill a request to the object that

options.text: has the necessary information to fulfill the request
is in control of the use case
has direct access to the database
is the expert of the application domain

explanation: The GRASP Information Expert pattern recommends assigning a responsibility to the class that possesses the necessary information to fulfill it. This leads to high cohesion and more maintainable designs.

text: The GRASP Expert pattern recommends assigning a responsibility to an object that:

options.text: has the data needed to perform the responsibility
can derive the required information from its own private data
minimizes coupling by centralizing all logic in one class

explanation: The GRASP Information Expert pattern assigns responsibility to the class that has the necessary data or can derive it from its own information. It does not concern workflow coordination (Controller), user request handling, or centralizing all logic in one class.

text: Which one of the following is accomplished through a judicious use of the expert pattern?

options.text: Responsibility assignment to the appropriate classes
Allows a user to add new functionality to an existing object without altering its structure.

explanation: The GRASP Information Expert pattern focuses on assigning responsibilities to the classes that have the relevant information needed to fulfill them. This results in proper responsibility assignment and higher cohesion among classes.

text: Benefits of using polymorphism in an object-oriented program is stated by which of the following?

options.text: The number of methods in the associated classes
Number of subclasses needed to accomplish the same functionality
Number of conditionals in method invocation reduces
Coupling among the associated classes increases
Dependency among the associated classes increases

explanation: Polymorphism replaces conditional logic (such as if-else or switch statements) with dynamic method binding, thereby reducing the number of conditionals during method invocation. It does not increase coupling or dependency; in fact, it typically reduces them.

text: Which one of the following are not reasons for not embedding business logic in the user interface objects?

options.text: A user interface object associated with a use case may not live till the completion of the use case
A user interface object associated with a use case may get created only at a later point of time during the use case execution
Domain classes can not work without a middle tier
It may reduce the coherency of a user interface object
It is not possible to embed business logic in a user interface object

explanation: Business logic can technically be embedded in UI objects, so statement (e) is false. Domain classes also do not inherently require a middle tier to function, making (c) incorrect; hence neither is a valid reason for avoiding business logic in the user interface.

text: Creator pattern does not recommend object creation responsibility to be allocated to which of the following classes?

options.text: A class that is an inventory of objects of that are to be created.
A class that has the information needed to initialize the object to be created.
A class that is not an associated class
A class whose instance will be the primary client of the object to be created.
An entity class that would be commanded by the object to be created.

explanation: The GRASP Creator pattern suggests assigning object-creation responsibility to classes that have information, aggregate, or will primarily use the object. Classes unrelated to the object (c) or entities commanded by the created object (e) should not be assigned creation responsibility.

text: Pure fabrication pattern should not be recommended to address which of the following problems in a design?
explanation: The GRASP Pure Fabrication pattern is used to improve cohesion and reduce coupling by introducing non-domain helper classes. It is not intended to solve violations of the Open/Closed Principle (OCP) or the Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP), which deal with extensibility and abstraction rather than class responsibility assignment.

text: The term "Delegation" most closely describes the theme of which one of the following GRASP patterns?
explanation: In GRASP, Delegation refers to assigning responsibility to another object to perform a task. The Controller pattern delegates the handling of system events (like user actions) to appropriate objects, rather than having the UI or client manage everything directly. This is a clear application of delegation.

text: Which one of the following sentences describes the Observer pattern most accurately?

options.text: This pattern is used to get a way to access the elements of a collection object in a sequential manner without any need to know its underlying representation.
This pattern is used to reduce communication complexity between multiple objects or classes.
This pattern provides a way to evaluate an arithmetic expression.
This pattern is primarily used to reduce the number of objects created
This pattern is used when there is one-to-many relationship between objects such as if one object is modified, its dependent objects are to be notified automatically.

explanation: The Observer pattern defines a one-to-many dependency between objects so that when the subject changes state, all its observers are automatically notified and updated. This is the core intent of the pattern.

text: Which one of the following GRASP design patterns can be used to improve the following code? public class MusicBand { private Singer singer; private Drummer drummer; private Guitarist guitarist; public Guitarist getGuitarist(){ return guitarist;} }
explanation: The code exposes internal objects (Guitarist) directly via a getter. This violates the Law of Demeter, which advises that a class should only talk to its immediate friends and not reach through objects to access their internals. Applying this principle would improve encapsulation and reduce coupling. c lass TourPromoter { public static void main(String args){ … guitaristName = band.getGuitarist().getName(); … }

text: Which of the following vexing problems might be faced during the development and maintenance of a software, if an application that you have designed violates the “Law of Demeter” GRASP pattern?
explanation: Violating the Law of Demeter not only increases coupling (a), but also makes the system harder to maintain (b). When classes are tightly coupled, a change in one class can ripple through others, raising maintenance effort and costs. So both a and b are correct effects of violating this GRASP principle.

text: Which one of the following statements is not true of the façade design pattern?

options.text: Use of façade class in a server package reduces the overall coupling in the design of a client-server system
Use of façade class in a server package increases the overall cohesion of the classes in the server package
The façade class often does little more than just delegating requests to other classes inside the package.
A façade class provides a common interface to the services offered by the classes of the package

explanation: The Façade pattern simplifies access to a subsystem by providing a unified interface, but it does not inherently change the cohesion of the classes within the subsystem. Cohesion depends on how closely related the responsibilities of the classes are, not on the presence of a façade. The other statements correctly describe façade behavior.

text: Which one of the following describes the Facade pattern correctly?

options.text: This pattern allows a user to add new functionality to an existing object without altering its class
This pattern is used where we need to treat a group of objects of different classes in a similar way, that is as the same object
This pattern hides the complexities of the system and provides an interface to the client using which the client can access the system
This pattern is primarily used to reduce the number of objects created and to decrease memory footprint and increase performance

explanation: The Facade pattern provides a simplified interface to a complex subsystem, allowing clients to interact with the system without needing to understand its internal complexity. It is primarily about abstraction and simplification, not object creation or treating multiple objects uniformly.

text: In a Java implementation of the Observer pattern, which one of the following is a suitable data structure for the Observable to maintain the references to the observers?
explanation: In the Observer pattern, the Observable needs to maintain an ordered collection of observers to notify them when its state changes. ArrayList is suitable because it allows dynamic resizing and sequential iteration over observers, which is required to notify each observer in turn. While Set could avoid duplicates, ArrayList is the conventional choice in Java implementations.

text: Bloated controller classes need to be split into two or more controller classes. This can be considered to be an application of which one of the following GRASP design patterns?
explanation: Splitting a bloated controller into multiple controllers introduces a non-domain class to handle responsibilities and improve cohesion or reduce coupling. This is an example of the Pure Fabrication pattern, which encourages creating a class solely for design reasons rather than representing a real-world entity.

text: Law of Demeter design pattern does not recommend a method call to which one of the following types of objects?

options.text: An object parameter of the method
An object that is an attribute of a called method

explanation: The Law of Demeter advises that a method should only call: 1. Itself (this or self) 2. Its method parameters 3. Its own attributes 4. Objects it creates It should not “reach through” another object to call a method on an object returned by that object (i.e., an attribute of a called method). This prevents tight coupling and preserves encapsulation.

text: Consider the following class diagram of the compiler sub-system of an application. What can be said about the role of the compiler class in the package?
explanation: In the given diagram, the compiler acts as a facade for the compiler subsystem classes.

text: Which one of the following GOF design patterns has been applied in the code snippet below? public class Logger { private static Logger logger; private Logger() { } public static Logger getLogger() { if (logger == null) { logger = new Logger(); } return logger; } public void log(String message) { System.out.println("LOG: " + message); } }
explanation: The Logger class restricts instantiation to one object using a private constructor and a static getLogger() method. This ensures global access to a single instance, which is the essence of the Singleton pattern.

text: In order to implement the Singleton design pattern, which of the following steps are essential?

options.text: The class must contain exactly one public constructor
The constructor should be declared private
The class must store its sole instance in a static attribute
The class must implement the Cloneable interface
A public static method should provide access to the single instance
The class must be marked as final to prevent inheritance

explanation: A Singleton requires a private constructor to prevent external instantiation, a static attribute to hold the single instance, and a public static method to provide access to that instance. Other steps, like final or Cloneable, are optional.

text: Which of the following characteristics of a class indicate the applicability of the Singleton pattern?

options.text: The class has only a single member method.
The class has only a single field.
The class should have exactly one instance.
The class can at most be subclassed once.
The class must provide a global access point to its sole instance.

explanation: The Singleton pattern is applicable when a class must have exactly one instance (c) and provides a global access point to that instance (e). Other characteristics like number of methods, fields, or subclassing are irrelevant.

text: Which one of the following describes the State pattern most accurately?

options.text: In this pattern, the behaviour of a class changes based on the specific algorithm that gets selected in a decision statement.
In this pattern, when the state of an object changes, it appears as if the object changed its class
In this pattern, a class behaviour or its algorithm can be changed at run time by the user.
In this pattern, the state behaviour of an object is implemented by internally encoding the states as algorithms.
In this pattern, an abstract class exposes defined ways to execute its methods

explanation: The State pattern allows an object to alter its behavior when its internal state changes, making it seem as if the object changes its class. This enables state-specific behavior without using complex conditional statements.

text: Which of the following are participants in the GoF State design pattern?
explanation: The State pattern has the following participants: Context - maintains a reference to the current state. State - defines the interface for state-specific behavior. ConcreteState - implements behavior specific to a particular state. Other options like Situation or Transition are not part of the standard GoF State pattern.

text: Consider the following structure of a singleton class. Which of the following are not essential to the satisfactory working of the singleton class?
explanation: The parts essential for a Singleton are the static uniqueInstance to hold the single instance, the static getInstance() method to provide global access, and the private constructor to prevent external instantiation. Other members like singletonData do not need to be static or private for the Singleton to function correctly; their accessibility or static nature depends on the design requirements, not the Singleton pattern itself.

text: Following Java code for a Singleton class has been written by a programmer. The singleton does not work satisfactorily as there is bug in the code. Which line in the code has the bug?
explanation: · In a correct singleton, getInstance() should create a new instance only if one does not exist. · Currently, line 5 always creates a new instance, ignoring whether uniqueInstance already exists. This breaks the singleton principle.

text: Which of the following pattern is used where we need to treat a group of objects in similar way as a single object?
explanation: The Composite pattern allows you to treat individual objects and compositions of objects uniformly. It is used to represent part-whole hierarchies, so clients can work with single objects and groups of objects in the same way.

text: Consider a watch that can toggle the display of time between analog or digital modes when the user presses a toggle switch on the watch. Which one of the following is the most accurate class model of the watch obtained by applying the state pattern.
explanation: Diagram C depicts most correctly the description provided in the questions.

text: Which one of the following is the main objective of the Singleton pattern?

options.text: Ensure that no more than one instance of a class exists.
Ensure that only one instance of a class exists for each thread of access.
Separate the objects of a single class from objects of another class.
Control the creation of the first instance of the classes to enhance efficiency.

explanation: The main objective of the Singleton pattern is to ensure that only one instance of a class exists throughout the application and provide a global point of access to it. This prevents multiple object creation and maintains consistent state across the system.

text: Which of the following are participants in the GOF Adapter design pattern?
explanation: In the Adapter pattern, Adapter converts an existing class (Adaptee) to match the Target interface expected by clients, allowing incompatible interfaces to work together. “Bridge” and “Old Interface” are unrelated to this pattern.

text: What are the consequences of applying the GOF Adapter pattern?

options.text: It makes the client code easier to understand as all interactions are carried out through interactions with a single uniform interface
It wraps the adaptee class with a different inrerface
It establishes a flexible mechanism for instantiating an object
It enables a client to use an incompatible server class

explanation: The Adapter pattern wraps the adaptee class with a new interface (c) and allows a client to use an incompatible class (e), enabling seamless integration without changing existing code.

text: Which one of the following design patterns is known as Surrogate pattern?
explanation: The Proxy pattern is also known as the Surrogate pattern because it provides a placeholder or representative for another object to control access to it.

text: When would you use the GOF Composite design pattern?

options.text: To decouple an abstraction from its implementation so that the two can vary independent
To translates an existing class interface into a compatible target interface
To arrange an object hierarchy such that the client code can access both the individual objects and the hierarchy in a uniform manner
To improve the system overall performance

explanation: You would use the Composite pattern to organize objects into a tree structure so that clients can treat individual objects and compositions uniformly. This simplifies client code when dealing with part-whole hierarchies.

text: Which one of the following sentences best defines the use of the Composite Design Pattern?

options.text: The Composite design pattern allows the clients to build a complex object from smaller different ones
It helps to decouple an abstraction from its implementation so that the two can vary independent
The Composite design pattern allows the clients to treat individual objects and compositions uniformly
The composite design pattern allows to incompatible classes to work
The Composite design pattern establishes a flexible mechanism for instantiating objects

explanation: The Composite pattern lets clients treat single objects and groups of objects in the same way, providing a uniform interface for both. This is useful for representing part-whole hierarchies without complicating client code.

text: In which of the following situations would you use the GOF Adapter design pattern?

options.text: To translate an existing class to interface to a compatible target interface
To extend the functionalities of client class
To allow a client class to work with a server class having an incompatible interface

explanation: You would use the Adapter pattern to allow a client class to work with a server class that has an incompatible interface (d), essentially translating the existing class interface to a form the client can use (a).

text: Which of the following are the common implementation strategies of the GOF Adapter pattern?
explanation: The common implementation strategies of the Adapter pattern are: Class Adapter - Uses inheritance to adapt one interface to another. Object Adapter - Uses composition to wrap an adaptee and present the target interface.

text: Proxy Pattern can be used to achieve which of the following?

options.text: Control access to a remote object
Assemble a set of smaller objects into complex objects
Instantiate a resource-intensive object when its service is requested by a client
Facilitate traversal of tree structures of arbitrary depth recursively
Enable a client to seamlessly access some remote service by providing the connection logic needed

explanation: The Proxy pattern provides a surrogate or placeholder for another object, controlling access to it and adding additional functionality without changing the original object. It can delay the creation of resource-intensive objects until they are actually needed, improving efficiency. It also handles remote access, allowing clients to interact with a service seamlessly while encapsulating the connection or access logic. This makes client code simpler and more secure.

text: Which design pattern you would you use to translate an existing class interface for using an incompatible target interface?
explanation: To translate an existing class interface to a compatible target interface, you would use the Adapter design pattern, which allows a client to work with a class that has an incompatible interface without modifying the existing code.

text: The bridge design pattern is useful to remedy which one of the following types of problems in a design?
explanation: The Bridge pattern is used to decouple an abstraction from its implementation, allowing both to vary independently. This addresses the violation of the Open/Closed Principle (OCP) by enabling extensions without modifying existing code.

text: Which one of the following statements is FALSE regarding the Proxy pattern?

options.text: A Proxy controls access to another object and may provide additional behavior such as caching or security checks.
A Proxy implements the same interface as the real subject so that the client can interact with it transparently.
A Proxy must always provide exactly the same concrete implementation of operations as the real subject.
A Remote Proxy can represent an object located on a different address space or network.
A Virtual Proxy may create expensive objects only on demand, delaying instantiation until necessary.

explanation: A Proxy implements the same interface as the real subject so clients can use it transparently, but it does not need to replicate the internal implementation of the real subject—it can add access control, caching, or lazy initialization instead.

text: Which one of the following statements is FALSE concerning the Facade pattern?

options.text: A Facade hides the complexity of multiple subsystems behind a simplified interface.
A Facade typically exposes a single high-level entry point to a set of operations.
A Facade adds new behavior to an object by dynamically wrapping it at runtime.
A Facade makes a subsystem easier to use without modifying the subsystem itself.
A Facade may internally coordinate multiple subsystem objects to complete a request.

explanation: This describes the Decorator pattern, not Facade. The Facade pattern provides a simplified interface to a complex subsystem without changing or dynamically wrapping the subsystem objects.

text: Which one of the following best describes the purpose of the Facade design pattern?

options.text: It provides a unified and simplified interface to a group of related subsystems.
It adapts an existing class interface to match another interface expected by the client.
It creates objects without exposing instantiation logic to the client.
It dynamically adds new responsibilities to an object at runtime.
It controls access to another object and may add security or lazy instantiation.

explanation: The Facade design pattern is used to provide a unified and simplified interface to a group of related subsystems, making the subsystem easier to use and reducing client-subsystem coupling.

text: Which Design Pattern should you use when you want to add responsibilities to individual objects dynamically and transparently without affecting other objects?
explanation: We should use the Decorator pattern when you need to add responsibilities to individual objects dynamically and transparently, without changing or affecting other objects of the same class.

text: A media-processing system supports several media types such as audio, video, and images. Each media type can be stored in multiple formats, such as local file, cloud object storage, or streamed over a network. The design should allow new media types or new storage mechanisms to be introduced independently without modifying the existing code. Which design pattern best fits this requirement?
explanation: The requirement is to decouple media types (audio, video, images) from storage mechanisms (local, cloud, streaming) so that both can evolve independently. The Bridge pattern is specifically intended for this kind of abstraction-implementation separation.

text: Consider a text editor in which a basic text view object is responsible for simply displaying plain text. Additional features such as scroll bars, line numbers, spell checking, and syntax highlighting may be dynamically added to the text view, depending on user choice, without modifying the original text view class. Which design pattern is most suitable in this scenario?
explanation: This scenario requires dynamically adding multiple, optional responsibilities to an object at runtime without modifying the original class. The Decorator pattern is designed exactly for this purpose.

text: Suppose you have developed a students’ grading software. The Grade information shared by teachers and students. However, only the teachers should be able to post and modify grades. Which one of the following design patterns will help you to achieve this in the most meaningful way?
explanation: The requirement is to control access to grade modification functionality, allowing teachers full access while restricting students to read-only access. The Proxy pattern is well suited for enforcing such access control by acting as a protective intermediary.

text: Consider a distributed system in which client objects need access to a remote database object located on a different machine. The database object is expensive to load and its methods involve network communication. In order to avoid exposing these communication details to client objects, and to control access to the remote object transparently, which one of the following design patterns should be used?
explanation: In this scenario, clients need transparent access to a remote, expensive object while hiding network communication details and controlling access. The Proxy pattern, specifically a Remote Proxy, is designed to handle exactly this requirement.

text: Which of the following pattern allows a user to add new functionality to an existing object without altering its structure?
explanation: The Decorator pattern allows new functionality to be added dynamically to an existing object without changing its structure or class. It wraps the object and extends its behavior transparently.

text: Which one of the following sentences describes the Iterator pattern most accurately?

options.text: This pattern is used to get a way to access the elements of a collection object in sequential manner without any need to know its underlying representation.
This pattern is used to reduce communication complexity between multiple objects or classes.
This pattern provides a way to evaluate an arithmetic expression.
This pattern is primarily used to reduce the number of objects created
This pattern is used when there is one-to-many relationship between objects such as if one object is modified, its dependent objects are to be notified automatically.

explanation: The Iterator pattern is used to access the elements of a collection sequentially without exposing the collection’s internal representation. This allows traversal to be decoupled from the underlying data structure.

text: In multiple linear regression $Y = X\beta + \epsilon$, if the design matrix $X$ has linearly dependent columns (multicollinearity), what is the primary numerical consequence?

options.text: $X^T X$ is non-invertible (singular), making the standard OLS closed-form solution $(\beta = (X^T X)^{-1}X^T Y)$ undefined.
The residual sum of squares becomes strictly zero.
The bias of the OLS estimator becomes infinite while variance vanishes.
The gradient descent algorithm will always diverge regardless of learning rate.

explanation: When features are collinear, the matrix $X^T X$ does not have full rank, meaning $\det(X^T X) = 0$. Hence $(X^T X)^{-1}$ does not exist, causing standard ordinary least squares estimates to fail or have extreme variance.

text: Which of the following statements comparing Ridge Regression (L2) and Lasso Regression (L1) are TRUE?

options.text: Lasso performs feature selection by shrinking some regression coefficients exactly to zero.
Ridge regression has an analytical closed-form solution: $\hat{\beta} = (X^T X + \lambda I)^{-1} X^T Y$.
Ridge regression forces coefficients to zero when $\lambda \to \infty$ but never at finite $\lambda$.
L1 penalty contour is circular/spherical in weight space while L2 is diamond-shaped.

explanation: Statements A, B, and C are true. D is inverted: the L1 constraint region is diamond-shaped with sharp corners along coordinate axes (inducing sparsity), whereas L2 is circular/hyperspherical.

text: In k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) classification, as the parameter $k$ increases towards the total dataset size $N$ ($k \to N$), how do bias and variance behave?
explanation: When $k=1$, the model has lowest bias but highest variance (overfitting). As $k$ grows large ($k \to N$), the decision boundary becomes very smooth (predicting majority class everywhere), leading to high bias and low variance.

sources: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, Bishop

text: Consider a Boolean function of 3 inputs $(x_1, x_2, x_3)$ that outputs 1 if and only if at least two of the inputs are 1 (Majority Function). Can this function be implemented by a single Perceptron with a step activation function?

options.text: Yes, because the majority function is linearly separable with weights $w_1=w_2=w_3=1$ and threshold $\theta=1.5$.
No, because any boolean logic beyond AND requires at least two hidden layers.
No, majority function is isomorphic to XOR and not linearly separable.
Yes, but only if an RBF kernel mapping is applied first.

explanation: The 3-input majority function is linearly separable: with $w_1=w_2=w_3=1$ and threshold $1.5$, $\sum w_i x_i \ge 2$ when 2 or 3 inputs are 1 (output 1), and $\le 1$ when 0 or 1 inputs are 1 (output 0).

sources: Neural Networks for Pattern Recognition, Bishop

text: For a trained soft-margin SVM with slack variables $\xi_i$, which points are considered Support Vectors?

options.text: Points on the margin ($y_i(w^T x_i + b) = 1, \xi_i = 0$) and points violating the margin ($0 < y_i(w^T x_i + b) < 1, \xi_i > 0$ or misclassified).
Only points strictly outside the margin ($y_i(w^T x_i + b) > 1$).
Only points where the slack variable $\xi_i$ equals exactly 0.
All points in the training set regardless of position.

explanation: In SVM, support vectors correspond to Lagrange multipliers $\alpha_i > 0$. By KKT conditions, this includes points lying exactly on the margin hyperplanes ($y_i f(x_i)=1$) as well as non-margin support vectors inside the margin or misclassified ($\xi_i > 0$).

text: The graph of data points shows a nonlinear strictly increasing curve that becomes steeper as $x$ increases, convex upward. Which mathematical form best characterizes this relationship among candidate models?

options.text: $y = e^{w x}$ or $y = x^w$ ($w > 1$) (Exponential/Power growth model)

explanation: A curve that is convex upward and increases at an accelerating rate is modeled by an exponential or super-linear power curve. Linear and log curves do not accelerate upwards.

text: Calculate the total number of trainable parameters (weights + biases) for a fully connected feed-forward neural network with: 5 input variables, 1 hidden layer with 3 neurons, and 1 output neuron for binary classification. (Each neuron has an independent bias).
explanation: Input to Hidden layer: 5 inputs * 3 hidden neurons = 15 weights, plus 3 biases = 18 parameters. Hidden to Output layer: 3 hidden outputs * 1 output neuron = 3 weights, plus 1 bias = 4 parameters. Total parameters = 18 + 4 = 22.

sources: Neural network architecture parameter counting formula

text: For a normal distribution with unknown mean $\mu$ and known variance $\sigma^2$, the maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) of $\mu$ is the sample mean. Given 5 observed sample marks: 25, 55, 64, 7, 99. Compute the MLE value of $\mu$.

sources: MLE sample mean of Gaussian distribution

text: In a neural network with squared error loss $E = (f - y)^2$, network output $f = 0.8176$, target $y = 5$, and derivative $\frac{\partial f}{\partial w_2} = 0.0746$. For initial weight $w_2 = 1.0$ and learning rate $\eta = 0.5$, calculate the updated weight $w_2^{(new)}$ after one gradient descent step.
explanation: Gradient $\frac{\partial E}{\partial w_2} = 2(f - y) \frac{\partial f}{\partial w_2} = 2(0.8176 - 5)(0.0746) = 2(-4.1824)(0.0746) \approx -0.6240$. Update rule: $w_2^{(new)} = w_2 - \eta \frac{\partial E}{\partial w_2} = 1.0 - 0.5(-0.6240) = 1.0 + 0.3120 = 1.3120$ (file gives 1.3119 due to intermediate rounding).

text: Which of the following statements comparing Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Support Vector Machines (SVM) are CORRECT?

options.text: ANN error surface is generally non-convex with multiple local minima and saddle points, while standard SVM optimization is convex with a unique global optimum.
After training, an ANN might land on a different minimum each time depending on random weight initialization.
A standard linear SVM can learn a decision boundary for arbitrary distributions without kernel trick.
ANNs are typically trained using backpropagation and gradient descent, whereas SVMs are solved using quadratic programming / convex optimization solvers.

explanation: Statements A, B, and D are correct. C is false because standard linear SVM produces only a flat linear hyperplane separator; handling arbitrary non-linear distributions requires non-linear kernels.

text: Given a binary confusion matrix with True Positives $TP = 6$, False Negatives $FN = 3$, False Positives $FP = 2$, True Negatives $TN = 9$. Calculate the Recall (Sensitivity) of the classifier. (Round to 2 decimal places).
explanation: $\text{Recall} = \frac{TP}{TP + FN} = \frac{6}{6 + 3} = \frac{6}{9} \approx 0.6667 \approx 0.67$.

text: In a 20-fold cross-validation scheme applied to a dataset of $N = 1000$ samples, how many samples are used in the training set for each fold?
explanation: For $k=20$ folds on 1000 samples, each validation fold contains $1000 / 20 = 50$ samples. The remaining training data consists of $1000 - 50 = 950$ samples (or $\frac{19}{20} \times 1000 = 950$).

text: What is the standard and mathematically correct definition of classification Accuracy from a binary confusion matrix?
explanation: Accuracy is defined as the total number of correct predictions divided by the total number of predictions: $\frac{TP + TN}{TP + TN + FP + FN}$. NOTE: The original assignment sheet contained a typo with factor 2, which our AI Answer Finder flagged as a CONFLICT.

text: Which of the following statements regarding Bagging (Bootstrap Aggregation) are TRUE?

options.text: Bagging primarily reduces variance without significantly increasing bias.
If the base classifiers are fully correlated, bagging provides no variance reduction benefit.
Bagging works by sequentially re-weighting misclassified instances.
Bagging is particularly effective when applied to unstable, high-variance learners like unpruned decision trees.

explanation: A, B, and D are true. Variance of an average of $B$ models with correlation $\rho$ and variance $\sigma^2$ is $\rho \sigma^2 + \frac{1-\rho}{B}\sigma^2$. When $\rho = 1$, the variance remains $\sigma^2$ (no reduction). C describes Boosting (e.g. AdaBoost), not Bagging.

text: Standard decision trees recursively partition the input feature space using single-feature threshold tests (e.g., $x_j < c$). What geometric regions do these recursive splits form in multidimensional feature space?

options.text: Convex Voronoi polygons with arbitrary orientations

explanation: Because each decision boundary is orthogonal to one of the coordinate feature axes ($x_j = c$), the recursive partitions form axis-parallel rectangular regions (hyper-rectangles in $\mathbb{R}^d$).

text: As the maximum depth of a decision tree increases, how do the training bias and variance of the model typically change?

options.text: Both Bias and Variance remain unchanged

explanation: A deeper tree has greater capacity to fit complex decision boundaries, reducing bias on the training set, but becomes highly sensitive to perturbations in the training data, increasing variance.

sources: Machine Learning: A Probabilistic Perspective, Murphy

text: For a classification tree evaluating candidate split points on a continuous feature, the weighted Gini impurities are computed as follows: Split 172.6 has Gini 0.2857; Split 176.35 has Gini 0.3200; Split 178.45 has Gini 0.4167; Split 185.4 has Gini 0.3750. What is the value of the optimal (minimum) weighted Gini impurity?
explanation: Decision trees choose the split that minimizes impurity (or maximizes impurity reduction). Comparing the values: $\min(0.2857, 0.3200, 0.4167, 0.3750) = 0.2857$ at split point 172.6.

text: What fundamental independence assumption does the Naive Bayes classifier make?

options.text: Features are conditionally independent given the class label: $P(X_1, \dots, X_n \mid Y) = \prod_{i=1}^n P(X_i \mid Y)$.
Features are mutually independent regardless of class label: $P(X_1, \dots, X_n) = \prod_{i=1}^n P(X_i)$.
The class labels are uniformly distributed: $P(Y=c) = 1/K$.
The features and target variable are linearly correlated.

explanation: The core assumption of Naive Bayes is class-conditional independence: given the class label $Y$, the attributes $X_1, X_2, \dots, X_n$ are conditionally independent.

sources: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, Bishop Ch. 4

text: Consider a Naive Bayes model where target $Y$ is Boolean (2 classes), feature $X_1$ is categorical with 3 possible values, and feature $X_2$ is continuous and modeled with a Gaussian distribution (mean and variance per class). How many total independent parameters must be estimated to specify this model?
explanation: 1) Prior $P(Y)$: Boolean requires $2 - 1 = 1$ parameter. 2) Categorical $X_1$: For each of the 2 classes, 3 categories require $3 - 1 = 2$ parameters: $2 \times 2 = 4$ parameters. 3) Gaussian $X_2$: For each of the 2 classes, Gaussian requires mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$: $2 \times 2 = 4$ parameters. Total = $1 + 4 + 4 = 9$ parameters.

text: In sequential boosting algorithms such as AdaBoost, what happens to the weights assigned to training instances that were misclassified by the current weak learner?

options.text: Their weights are increased, forcing subsequent weak learners to concentrate on difficult samples.
Their weights are set to zero and pruned from subsequent iterations.
Their weights are decreased so that easy samples dominate convergence.
Their weights remain fixed, only the learner voting coefficient changes.

explanation: AdaBoost increases the sample distribution weight $w_i^{(t+1)} = w_i^{(t)} e^{\alpha_t}$ for misclassified examples (where $y_i h_t(x_i) = -1$), prioritizing them in the next weak learner's objective function.

text: In a Random Forest with $p$ total features, each split considers a random subset of $m$ features ($m < p$). Which of the following statements about tuning $m$ are TRUE?

options.text: Decreasing $m$ reduces correlation between individual trees in the forest.
Increasing $m$ generally increases the individual strength/accuracy of each individual tree.
Setting $m = p$ makes the Random Forest completely identical to standard Bagging of trees.
Decreasing $m$ always guarantees a reduction in both bias and variance simultaneously.

explanation: A, B, and C are correct. Smaller $m$ produces less correlated trees (reducing forest variance) at the cost of slightly higher individual tree bias. When $m = p$, every feature is available at every split, which is exactly standard Bagging. D is false because reducing $m$ typically increases bias slightly.
